Selection-frequency aggregation of the between-response graph structure

Source: R/selection.R
mc_graph_stability.Rd

Repeats graph selection in B half-samples and records the empirical selection frequency \(\hat\Pi_e\) of every edge, the proportion of valid subsamples in which the selector retains it. Edges with \(\hat\Pi_e\ge\pi_{\mathrm{thr}}\) are returned as recurrent. The frequency estimates the probability that the selector retains the edge in a random half-sample; it is not the probability that the edge belongs to the graph. With a selector tuned by an information criterion, the default, the procedure is a diagnostic aggregation scheme and not the error-controlled stability selection of Meinshausen and Buehlmann (2010), because the number of edges each subsample selects is not controlled: the recurrent set then carries no formal bound on its false selections. Passing q gives the version for which such a bound is reported, under the conditions stated below.

Usage

mc_graph_stability(
  fit,
  B = 100L,
  pi_thr = 0.6,
  method = c("stepwise", "penalized"),
  criterion = "bic",
  refit = c("residual", "full"),
  workers = 1L,
  cluster = NULL,
  q = NULL,
  sampling = c("half", "complementary"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_stability'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" (GGM layer).

B

number of subsamples (default 100); with sampling = "complementary", the number of pairs, so \(2B\) subsamples are drawn.

pi_thr

selection-frequency threshold in \([0,1]\) (default 0.6).

method

per-subsample selector: "stepwise" (mc_graph_stepwise, default) or "penalized" (mc_select_lambda). It is set to "penalized" when q is given.

criterion

information criterion passed to the selector ("bic", the default, "aic", "qic", "gbic", its alias "clbic", or "ebic"); not used when q is given.

refit

"residual" (default) resamples the stored Pearson residuals with the first stage held fixed; "full" resamples rows of the data and refits both stages in every half-sample.

workers

number of parallel workers for the resampling loop. The subsamples are drawn in the parent before any dispatch, so a given seed yields the same subsamples at any worker count and the result does not depend on it. Sequential by default, deliberately: user code often parallelizes at an outer level, and nesting a second level of workers underneath oversubscribes the machine. Forking is used where available; on Windows the call falls back to sequential evaluation. Inside a parallel worker the argument is ignored, with a warning.

cluster

optional vector with one identifier per observational row; half of the clusters, rounded down, are drawn without replacement in every half-sample (at least two with sampling = "half", at least one per half with sampling = "complementary").

q

optional integer between 1 and \(R(R-1)/2\): the number of edges each subsample selects along the L1 path, which turns on the error-controlled procedure described above and requires method = "penalized" when method is given.

sampling

"half" (default), B independent half-samples drawn without replacement, or "complementary", B pairs of disjoint halves.

...

further arguments passed to the per-subsample selector (mc_graph_stepwise or mc_select_lambda); ignored when q is given. For the print method, ignored.

x

an object of class "mcg_stability".

Value

An object of class "mcg_stability" with the empirical selection-frequency matrix among valid subsamples (selection_prob), its conservative counterpart divided by all attempted subsamples (selection_prob_conservative), the numbers of valid and failed subsamples (B_valid, B_failed), and the recurrent edge set (stable_edges, a two-column matrix of the pairs whose frequency among valid subsamples is at least pi_thr). With q it also carries q and the error_bound, NA when pi_thr is not above one half. The list also records B, pi_thr, method, criterion, refit, sampling, clustered, n_subsamples and the data frame failures (subsample index and error message of each failed subsample). The matrices have the response names as dimnames and hold the frequency of each pair in both triangles. print returns its argument invisibly.

Stability selection with error control

With q, every subsample selects the first q edges to enter along the L1 path of mc_graph_penalized, run with warm starts over a geometric grid of 50 penalties from the value that zeroes every edge in that subsample, \(\lambda_{\max}\) (or \(10^{-3}\) if larger), down to \(10^{-3}\) times it; edges that enter at the same grid point are ranked by the size of their coefficient there. Grid points whose fit is not certified are skipped, and fewer than q edges are selected when fewer enter along the grid, so \(q\) is an upper limit on the number of edges per subsample. The expected number of falsely selected edges among those whose frequency reaches pi_thr is then bounded by Theorem 1 of Meinshausen and Buehlmann (2010), $$E(V)\le\frac{q^2}{(2\pi_{\mathrm{thr}}-1)\,|E_{\max}|},\qquad \tfrac12<\pi_{\mathrm{thr}}\le1,$$ where \(V\) is the number of falsely selected edges, \(q\) the number of edges each subsample selects and \(|E_{\max}|=R(R-1)/2\) the number of pairs, reported as error_bound. The bound rests on two conditions the package cannot check: the selection indicators of the null edges are exchangeable, and the selector is no worse than random guessing. It is a bound on an expected count, not on a probability, and it refers to frequencies computed over all the subsamples; when some subsamples fail, selection_prob_conservative is the frequency that counts a failed subsample as selecting no edge, whereas the recurrent set is read from the frequencies among the valid ones. With sampling = "complementary" the subsamples come in B pairs of disjoint halves, the complementary pairs of Shah and Samworth (2013). What the bound controls is the edges of the residual layer as the second stage sees them; with refit = "residual" the first stage is held fixed.

What each half-sample is

With refit = "residual" the half-sample is drawn from the stored Pearson residuals and the first stage is held fixed, so the frequencies describe the second stage alone. With refit = "full" the half-sample is drawn from the rows of the data, the first-stage MCGLM (multivariate covariance generalized linear model) is refitted on it, and the selector runs on the residuals of that refit, so the frequencies carry the variability of both stages. The second form accounts for the estimation of the first stage and costs an MCGLM fit per half-sample; the first is the default and is cheaper.

A half-sample holds \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) of the \(n\) rows, drawn without replacement, and at least two. With sampling = "complementary" one random permutation of the rows is split into two disjoint halves of \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) rows each (at least one), so that with \(n\) odd one row is left out of the pair.

With cluster, half of the clusters are drawn instead of half of the rows, under the same rounding and the same minimum sizes counted in clusters, and every row of a drawn cluster enters the half-sample. That is the form to use when the unit of dependence is a cluster of rows, and it is required with refit = "full" when the within-response structure is not the identity: each drawn cluster then keeps its own block of the structure, as in mc_graph_bootstrap.

References

Meinshausen, N. and Buehlmann, P. (2010). Stability selection. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 72(4), 417–473. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2010.00740.x

Shah, R. D. and Samworth, R. J. (2013). Variable selection with error control: another look at stability selection. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 75(1), 55–80. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2011.01034.x

See also

mc_graph_stepwise, mc_select_lambda, mc_graph_penalized.

Other structure selection: mc_edge_scores(), mc_graph_penalized(), mc_graph_stepwise(), mc_select_lambda()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 300
K <- diag(4)*2; K[1,2]<-K[2,1]<- -0.6; K[2,3]<-K[3,2]<- -0.6; K[3,4]<-K[4,3]<- -0.6
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * 4), n) %*% chol(solve(K)); x <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1=Y[,1], y2=Y[,2], y3=Y[,3], y4=Y[,4], x=x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1~x,y2~x,y3~x,y4~x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_graph_stability(f, B = 40)
#> Selection-frequency aggregation (stepwise, criterion = bic, B = 40, threshold = 0.60)
#> Half-samples: residuals resampled, first stage held fixed
#> Valid subsamples: 40 | failed: 0
#> Recurrent edges: 3
#> Edges:
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
#> [2,]    2    3
#> [3,]    3    4
#> 
#> Selection probabilities:
#>      y1   y2   y3   y4
#> y1 0.00 1.00 0.00 0.03
#> y2 1.00 0.00 1.00 0.05
#> y3 0.00 1.00 0.00 0.98
#> y4 0.03 0.05 0.98 0.00
# }
